name: The Table

reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=a month ago, review=There’s something truly special about The Table.

It’s one of those rare restaurants that manages to feel both familiar and surprising every single time. The space has an easy charm — elegant but not trying too hard — and the energy always feels just right, whether it’s lunch sunlight filtering through the windows or a lively dinner service.

The food is consistently beautiful in its simplicity. Every dish feels like it’s been thought through — fresh, balanced, and built around great produce rather than fuss. You can taste the confidence in the cooking. The menu reads globally, but the soul of it feels distinctly their own.

And the service — calm, intuitive, quietly excellent. It’s clear that a lot of care goes into every part of the experience.

After all these years, The Table still feels like one of the most assured, grown-up dining rooms in Mumbai — the kind of place you leave already planning your next visit., name_person=Nuzzy J}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservations recommended, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Moderate noise, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Wheelchair_accessibility, E:ACCESSIBILITY], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=Really enjoyed our meal at The Table, Mumbai. We started with fresh oysters, followed by the salmon and beef tartare, both well balanced and made with great quality ingredients. The French onion soup and corn bread were comforting and full of flavor.

The lobster was cooked perfectly and tasted excellent, and the beef fillet that followed was tender, well seasoned, and done just right. The atmosphere is relaxed yet refined, with attentive service throughout. A great place for a leisurely, well-executed meal—would happily return., name_person=Vishal Shah}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Varies by time/day, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Moderate noise, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[1_person, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_ONE], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=a week ago, review=Having conducted prior research on this establishment, I was eager to experience their signature offering.

Upon my arrival, I was promptly greeted by the hostess and escorted directly to the banquet table. After a brief period of settling in, I placed my order for the Spaghetti Nero. The dish was delivered approximately 15 minutes later.

The ingredients were notably fresh, the spaghetti was expertly seasoned, and the portion size was ample for one individual, or even one and a half.

Overall, this was an exceptional experience., name_person=Gaurav Bhandarkar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 months ago, review=Wow! Wow! This place lives up to its very high standards. Food, in particular, service and ambience. It’s all outstanding. I must admit I was trying to find something wrong with this place. Will come back for sure., name_person=Samriddhi Nandi}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 months ago, review=After 43 years my sister and I went out for dinner, just the two of us... no spouses, no kids, no grandkids! And what an evening it was! Perfect ambience, beautiful presentations, and above all, impeccable, friendly and very personal service!
A special shout out to Dhiraj who was the team member that attended to us. I am planning to take my wife there next time I'm back in Bombay and Dhiraj is a huge part of the reason for that ❤️!
Highly, highly recommend The Table., name_person=Mayank Vora}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 months ago, review=Incredible meal at The Table, can easily see why they're no 1.

Desserts are great as well., name_person=Sudarshan Pawar}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Good service, great ambience, quality, price and staff is worth it !}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Non Veg food is yummy eager hostess and servers to help you choose a good meal.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=A good selection of wines and whiskey on offer, but don't miss the cocktails}"]

It was a delightful afternoon spent with great cocktails and surprising fusion of flavors and concepts. We were a party of six, so we could experience a lot on the menu and barring perhaps a couple of the dishes, every other dish was simply delectable and yum! There isn’t a “one” dish that I can single out as the highlight, there were multiple of them. Among the cocktails we tried:
·         Tamarind Whisky Shake – just a hint of the sweet sourness from the tamarind to add the kick but did not lose the character of the whisky
·         Waiting List – Gin based, curry leaf salt flavored, quite innovative in terms of the flavors
·         Stranger cocktail – Refreshing and again flavor packed
For drinks we also had the IPA, Belgian Wit and a green apple mocktail (green flag). The beers were nice but the mocktail was ok, especially compared to the bursts of flavors we were experiencing from the other drinks. A lot of what we ate was all simply superb and sent us down a flavor packed, surprise filled road! I mean – who would have thunk “kadi patta khakra” can taste that good!!! (that comes with the carrot thoran btw). The Chive brioche that came with the squid kheema pao was so amazing that we asked for two extra portions of just the brioche! Buttery, fluffy and heavenly! The dishes we ate and loved: Garlic Sourdough Naan, Morning Glory, Squid Kheema Pao, Mutton claypot rice, malai kofta, chur chur paratha, avocado papdi chaat, carrot thoran, seyal Pao (chef’s kiss!!!), and sea bass sev puri.
On the flip side, some of the dishes in our opinion missed the mark or were simply not to our palate like the Prawn Malai Curry (felt very watery and one could only taste the galangal and not much else), Prawn Pani Puri (just felt like a bit of strange juxtaposition in terms of flavors) and the fish pulimunchi (which was good in terms of flavor but simply wasn’t pulimunchi). The Ghee roast kabab and the corn locho were not bad but felt quite flat and underwhelming.
Finally, do not miss the dessert! The Coffee Rasgulla Sundae is something else! I could eat an entire bowl of just the almond brittle in that dessert. Other desserts we ate and loved – Gadbad falooda, my uncle’s birthday cake and coconut phirni.
Our server Tilak was prompt, friendly and amazing with his recommendations. The service is quick and on point. Make sure to call ahead and reserve your table, especially if you plan to visit the place over the weekend. Valet parking is available., name_person=Kanchan Shetty}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=I first dined here on my birthday and that meal has been one of the top 5 of my life so far.

The food is new and comforting at the same time, like a vintage car with a brand new engine. The drinks are thought out and the cocktails might actually deserve their four-digit price tags. Have a chat with the bartender and he’ll explain where the liquor comes from, how long the flavor has to sit in a dungeon before being released, and maybe give you a taster if you’re nice enough.

Imagery aside:

- the food tastes great;
- the portions are surprisingly large for similar restaurants in Mumbai (which does make up for the price somewhat);
- the drinks are memorable (unless you have too many); and
- the ambience is fine - it’s on a busy Bandra street though so I think they’ve done well with what they had. You can still see Salt Water Café’s bones sticking through the walls (the place that was here before Bandra Born was…born)

All in all - I would and have and will recommend this place to my friends and family.

Overview
AER at the Four Seasons is a rooftop experience that lives up to the hype. Perched high above Worli, it delivers sweeping Mumbai skyline and sea views, a modern yet warm ambience, and consistently polished service — ideal for both special evenings and relaxed drinks with friends.

Ambience & design
- Incredible vantage point: panoramic views of Mumbai and the Arabian Sea are the star — especially dramatic when clouds roll in or the city lights up at night.
- Roof engineering: the covered rooftop feels state-of-the-art — thoughtfully designed to shelter guests during rain while preserving the sense of openness. Even in a downpour the space felt airy and comfortable, with rain adding to the drama rather than disrupting the experience.
- Vibe: stylish, contemporary décor with an upscale lounge energy. Music, lighting and layout encourage both intimate conversations and lively groups without feeling crowded.

Drinks
- Negroni: expertly executed — perfectly blanched (clean, balanced bitterness and bright aromatics), with excellent temperature and presentation. The cocktail showcased strong technique and attention to classic proportions.
- Cocktail program: creative but respectful of classics; bartenders clearly know their craft and tailor drinks to taste.

Food
- Guacamole prepared tableside: a highlight. Watching it made fresh added theatre, and the result was vibrant, aromatic and packed with flavour — creamy texture, bright citrus and just the right seasoning. Superb balance of richness and acidity.
- Overall tasting: dishes leaned modern, high-quality and well-seasoned. Portions are geared for sharing and designed to complement the cocktail-led experience.

Service
- Attentive and professional without being intrusive. Staff handled the evening smoothly, from timing of drinks and food to accommodating the rain cover without fuss.

- Polished, thoughtful service.

Cons / notes
- Popularity means it can get busy; reservations are recommended for prime seating.
- Price point is upscale — expect to pay a premium for the location and experience.

Who it’s for
- Couples seeking a romantic, skyline-backed evening.
- Groups celebrating special occasions.
- Cocktail enthusiasts who appreciate skilled bartending and well-executed classics.

Bottom line
AER at the Four Seasons is a standout rooftop destination in Mumbai. •	Gallops is located inside the Mahalaxmi Race Course in Mumbai, which gives it a uniquely lush, open-green backdrop uncommon in the city’s dining scene.  ￼

YONUS KHAN KA PANEER TIKKA - signature dish. Middle had a filling of dry fruits and nuts. Indian spices tandoor well with spices balanced
Subz gauloti - melt in mouth minced veggies with herbs and spices served over a bread. So Lucknow ( must try )
MALAI KA PHOOL - richness all over . Cheese and cream marinated broccoli charred.
Perfect

Non veg platter - Mahira babuli kebab famous dish of amritsar on bones. Melt in mouth tangy spicy marinating. Must try

Small portion of Subz Chilman biryani , long grain basmati rice with saffron a bit of Ittar ghee and veggies

Breads - Taftaan / Khameeri / Naan
However the dessert had a pleasant surprise
Had a capsicum halwa FOR the first time.
Something different which one needs to try out

Overall experience = awesome
Felt like a Nawab Dining at this place paired with a sparkling wine

Big thanks to Saurabh Dixit and team Westin for hosting

I visited the place today. Mocktails & appetizers were amazing. The vegetable dumplings were unique. Mr Yogesh, the manager, offered me personalised services; the other servers were equally helpful and absolutely friendly. The main Course was average - I tasted some French Beans and Chicken. In the deserts, the Wasabi Cheese Case was fantastic.

Visit 3 [ Extract ]

Some of the dishes I had:

Duck [ in the main course, whose precise name I don't remember ] - Unusually strong on species, very much unauthentic, some pieces covered almost entirely in bones, and tough to chew upon. Call it a botched preparation and mood spoiler! It's not very often that I leave behind any dish. The grievance was resolved amicably.

Pork baos - You don't get these in many same-level restaurants, so a must-try. On a sweeter side and minced well and soft to consume. Arrived in the estimated time.

The quantity for all the dishes was above average and probably the largest I have seen at same-level restaurants.

Visit 4

A supreme and unforgettable experience

Some of the dishes I tried:

Traditional Pecking Duck - A conventional Chinese dish which is usually served with pancakes, troika of sauces, some veggies, and ofcourse, the duck cuts. Kudos to the chef, on my request, for serving me ready-made and saving me all the effort. The dish was slightly on the sweeter side, and the rolls had a good proportion of duck. Much laborious to scoff if all constituents are served separately.

Steamed Chilean Sea Bass - Prepared in soya ginger sauce, lightly spicy, mildly  pungent, and medium in size. Delicious, healthy and a must try. Maybe a few veggies at the side should be considered.

Light Breeze mocktail - Indeed light, mild soda, simple as it gets. Kinda like virgin mojito less Sprite/7UP and less coriander.

Grapefruit-based mocktail - the best of the three, authentic grapefruit flavour with medium bitterness, preserving the original taste, no soda.

Watermelon-based mocktail - another light one with no soda, pure watermelon [ and no syrup ] and a dash of cucumber.

We should have be warned right after entering: no friendly hello from the staff and worst 90s pop songs played way too lout from a DJ (btw: who needs a DJ for that most mainstream unpersonal song selection?).

The interior design is kind of post modern Art Deco but far from being cozy or cool.
*But now for the drinks.*:
One of the reviewers praised them for the story that would be behind each of the signature drinks.
Well, the bar menu mentions a story for each signature drink. But there is no recognisable connection between the story and the drink.
And there is not even necessarily a connection between drink description and drink. Or would you expect a garden salad with plenty of cucumber seeds that fills one third of your glass when only white rum, vodka, lime and syrup are mentioned in the menu? And
One could overlook this, if the two signature drinks we had, would have convinced by creativity and taste. But they didn’t, not at all.
The best signature drinks become classics some day. A good signature drink makes you remember drink and location. These unbalanced drinks we won’t remember.

Specially The Saboot Lobster., name_person=Manasi Satam}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+}, time_line=10 months ago, review=Beware: 2365 rupee / £24.49 for a bowl of cumin rice/jeera rice!!! Our stay at ITC Grand Central was ruined by this restaurant experience.

We ordered one murgh tikka, lamb tawa, and 1 kashmiri roti, 1 paratha and one jeera rice (rice is NOT on the menu but we were able to order via the waiter). However our experience was totally dampened when we received the bill. The jeera rice was listed for 2635 rupees (we are from London and this equates to £24.50 for a bowl of rice). Ridiculous. We flagged to the waiter who confirmed this is the correct price. We requested the manager, who also confirmed its the correct price and asked how we would like to pay. We said no way are we paying for rice that expensive, charge us appropriately we said. He then went away for 10 minutes and came back with 15% off the rice. We were shocked to see the rice was still on the bill. We said no, the rice was not on the menu and they should charge us properly and appropriately for rice!! He said it is on the menu and we didn’t look properly. We then showed him the online menu from which we ordered from where not one single rice dish is mentioned and he said the menu must vary by device. He then went away for 10 minutes and came back with the rice removed. He mentioned that even he was shocked at the rice but the fact he didnt remove the rice from the bill in a 5 star hotel restaurant was very poor. He then asked if we were staying at the hotel and was shocked to hear that we were and then finally apologised for the bill. Very strange encounter. As we left he thanked is for highlighting the bill discrepancy and apologised. We believe we were overcharged on purpose. We normally charge dinners and extras to the room but were so glad we didnt in this case so we were able to notice the ridiculous price and the clear scamming of customers. Absolutely shocking. PLEASE BE WARY., name_person=Ishani}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,800–2,000}, time_line=2 years ago, review=One of the most exciting dinner of my trip in India!

Food

The menu boasts a variety of food options, including breakfast platters, which might initially seem impressive. However, the taste of the food is compromised and does not justify the high prices. For a cafe that markets itself as a premium experience, the quality of the dishes leaves much to be desired.

Ambience and Seating

The sitting space is one of the better aspects of Cafe Trofima. Considering it is a cafe, the seating is comfortable and suitable for casual conversations or work. However, the overall ambience is just average, with no music to elevate the vibe. It lacks the warmth or charm that many would expect from a cafe in this area.

Service

The service is satisfactory but nothing extraordinary. While the staff is polite and attends to customers in a timely manner, the overall experience doesn’t stand out as memorable.

Location and Accessibility

A significant downside is the lack of parking space, which can be a hassle, especially given the busy location of Shivaji Park. Visitors arriving in their own vehicles may find it inconvenient.

Pricing

The prices are on the higher side, making it hard to justify for the quality of food and overall experience provided. While there are plenty of food options to choose from, the value for money is not reflected in the offerings.

Verdict

Cafe Trofima is overrated and doesn’t quite live up to its reputation. While it has some redeeming qualities like decent seating and satisfactory service, the compromised food taste, lack of parking, and high prices make it hard to recommend wholeheartedly. It could work as a one-time visit for those curious about its breakfast platters, but better options are available in and around the area for a more satisfying experience.

The restaurant has an outdoor and indoor seating section and there's a small roof top section which I didn't explore. The ambiance of the place closely matches the Mexican vibes while it can seat people of all group sizes. At the very end of my meal, i saw they had kept board games as well! While the music playing in the background had good selection of western songs and not something the ones popularly played on Instagram reels these days, which is the case with certain restaurants.

The staff experience is good. Viraj was the one who assisted for the night, he was good at explaining the menu as well as mocktails. The dishes were handed out in a timely manner and nothing felt rushed.

Coming to the food, we ordered:
- Santa Fe Chicken Quesadilla: There was a good quantity of chicken filling, whereas the tortilla was grilled perfectly. It's a bit on the sweeter side but overall I liked it. Fries on the side were a big bonus.

- Chicken and Mushroom Buritto: This was Buritto wrap with chicken and mushroom in creamy sauce with rice served on the side. The cream sauce tasted really good while the Buritto wrap had a good quantity of chicken and mushroom. The quantity of ingredients was perfect which made it enjoyable. Rice was more Indianized and could have kept it less moist to make it more close to the original.

- Empanada: It was the chicken and cheese empanda but this one was the weakest of all. The fried dough was crisp but hardly any filling inside it, while being provided with mayo on the side, it didn't go well!

We also ordered a couple of mocktails, Miami vice which was a mixture of pineapple juice and some thing else which I don't remember, the coconut flavour in it elavated the drink. I went for fresh watermelon with basil leaves something.. and it was refreshing!

Overall a great experience, would definitely visit it again in the future!

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=Having lived and worked in Japan, albeit many moons ago, I was not expecting to be reminded of the tastes and feel of a typical izakaya in the land of the rising sun, in, of all places, Bandra, Mumbai.
We were ushered to our seating by a raucous welcome from the Kuuraku staff, which was more reminiscent of the Wankhede Stadium than a Japanese restaurant. But there was a effervescence about the staff at Kuuraku, reflecting the confidence that they have in their excellent food.
We ordered the Special Kushi Course, comprising 5 sticks of yakitori. The standout of this was the chicken tail. It was so good that we ordered two extra sticks of this, named bonjiri shio. We also ordered a portion of pork belly yakitori although this was very slightly disappointing as it was a little on the tough side. Another slight disappointment was the chargrilled asparagus wrapped in pork belly. Again, the pork belly wasn't as tender as I expected and the asparagus was a little small and fibrous. However, the edamame challenge was a lot of fun. The idea is to grab as much edamame as possible with one hand - and what you grab is what you get to eat. I used my goalkeeper hands to grab, what the server told me was an over par amount. The edamame was quite good too. The crunchy ebi roll was very generous too coming as a generous portion. The temperature of the rice was spot on as was the consistency. Could the quality of the rice be higher as in Japan? Well yes if you can get that rice but otherwise it really was excellent. The same goes for the pork rice. Here the consistency or the stickiness of the rice was more important than in the ebi roll and if they could get better rice it was be amazing. The slight disappointment was the inclusion of bell peppers. Heresy! Finally, the tea was served in a beautiful black pot, again, very true to Japan.
All in all this was an excellent place with a really true feel of Japan, helped also by the constant stream of Japanese music and the service was particularly excellent. reviews:
["{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=As the name suggests, a high end premium restaurant located in Atria Mall next to Matahari on level 4, South Bombay Bar was the place I wanted to revisit so eagerly. Had a fabulous experience last time around and it was no different this time around as well. I love the ambiance of the place, well spread, spacious, everyone gets their privacy, yet you always feel right in between action all the time. Just loved how they have painted the ceiling with the map of South Mumbai and well illuminated wall depicting CSTM building structure. A nice mix of high tables, couple tables, comfortable sofa seating, regular tables and chairs section for large groups, just a very well planned layout I must say.

Talking about what all I tried here at South Bombay Bar, I actually just loved everything that was called for -

We started with few appetizers - Mexican Potatoes, Cheese Chilli Garlic Bread and Cheesy Jalapeno Stuffed Mushrooms. I just loved all three of them, but a word of caution for the Mexican Potatoes. Extremely rich in flavours but the Mexican spices also do their wonder. So it's really spicy. We actually asked the chef to tone down the spices, but we still felt it was quite spicy. So those who are in love with spice, this is your treat. I am a big fan of mushrooms and when it's jalapeno and cheese stuffing, it's heavenly. Don't miss this if you eat mushrooms. Last but not the least, we feel you can't go wrong with a chilli cheese toast, but you need to get it right. And that's what you will get here, a safe bet Always.

Along with food, called for couple of drinks - one of my favorites again - Date and Saffron Frappe. I don't think you get this anywhere else and somewhere it's definitely worth travelling and coming here perhaps just for this. Must must try! Also tried the Rosemary Watermelon Iced Tea. Fresh Watermelon is always good to have and a nice blend by the bar tender. Moving on to the mains, we tried the Paneer Londonwala Meal (Tikka Masala gravy) and called for Parathas as our Indian bread option. Just loved this Paneer vegetable one of the best. Meal comes along with papad. Beautiful presentation! After this meal, we had the Dhabewali Dal Khichdi, perfectly made. Light on stomach.

Finally, for desserts - we had Sexin A Tea Pot! Interesting name but I was excited to have this gooey chocolate with vanilla Ice-cream and Orange Zest. It has a modern, chic vibe crossed with a vibrant and sassy decor, perfect for a date night, or for a hangout sesh with friends.

The decor feels inspired by Malay/Singaporean cafes, with a lot of the artwork depicting the same, and it comes off pretty well. They have both indoor and outdoor seating, though the indoor seating is a bit cramped, but that's mostly fine. They do have a small bar serving the usual suspects, as well as some of their own stuff.

While I didn't get to order a large chunk of their menu, whatever I had was pretty great. Their name is definitely apt, as the baos I got were plump and pillowy, and the filling was perfect. I got the pork char siu baos, and the pork was fatty and melt in your mouth, complimented nicely by a slice of raw apple, giving it a fruity kick. Every Bao order comes with two, making it perfect for date night.

I also got their raw papaya salad, which was one of the best renditions of the dish I've eaten in Mumbai. It was tangy, sweet and spicy in just the right amounts, and wasn't just a refreshing palate cleanser, but a great meal by itself. It's also a very generous portion making it great for sharing.

The last thing I got were Chicken and asparagus dumplings, which didn't impress me as much, as I've had better dumplings in the same price range. They weren't bad but not particularly great either. The filling was generous, but it lacked in flavor. For 6 pieces, it was not the best value, and I recommend trying other dumplings, or avoiding dumplings all together.

Overall, I would rate both the Char Siu Bao and the Papaya Salad a solid 9/10, and the dumplings about a 6.5/10. Definitely go for their baos( pretty obvious given their name).

The service was fine, but they do tend to ignore the smaller tables and focus on the bigger groups, and it was also pretty busy on the day I visited. But I did see other tables also not receiving food at the proper times, so I'd rate the service a little lower, like a 6/10. Definitely could do with some improvement.

The Fatty Bao definitely ticks a lot of the boxes, though they do miss a little bit in their service, and cocktail variety, though I did not have the opportunity to try it. However, they more than make up for it with their snazzy decor and contemporary vibe, along with some pretty great food. I highly recommend checking the place out if you're out shopping in Linking Road and need to grab some lunch or dinner. You're definitely gonna be leaving a happy and fatty bao when you're done.

Located in the heart of Andheri West, Kofuku is a stunning blend of aesthetics and authenticity. With its serene ambiance and traditional touches, it offers a beautiful space to unwind — ideal for a romantic evening or a relaxed outing with friends. The interiors reflect a calming Japanese charm, complete with minimalist décor and warm lighting, setting the mood for a culturally rich dining experience.

🍸 Drinks: A Sensory Delight
We began our meal with some exceptional cocktails and mocktails:

Kimchi Kick Cocktail – A perfect balance of flavor and spice with impressive presentation. It stood out not only for its bold taste but also for the creative way it was served. My friend absolutely loved it too.
Buddha Bliss – Unique and refreshing, this cocktail brought together subtle flavors in a truly blissful mix.
Sakura (Mocktail) – Visually stunning and light on the palate, this mocktail was a favorite for its floral notes and elegant presentation.
Pinku no Yokubo – Another standout, both in taste and aesthetics. A must-try if you're looking for something different.
🍣 Starters & Sushi: Art on a Plate
Ebi Tempura Roll Sushi – This was a highlight. The presentation was elegant, and the tempura was perfectly crisp. The flavors were balanced and absolutely delicious.
Rock Shrimp – Cooked to perfection, juicy and flavorful. This dish had a great texture and was well-seasoned.
Tteokbokki Chicken – A Korean classic done right. Spicy, chewy, and flavorful with a presentation that matched its taste.
🍛 Main Course: Flavorful & Filling
Chef’s Special Japanese Curry – Rich, comforting, and beautifully presented. The curry had depth and warmth — everything you'd expect from a chef’s signature dish.
Korean-Style Chicken Mandu – These dumplings were unique in flavor, with a perfect outer texture and a delicious filling inside. A great introduction to Korean appetizers.
Korean Stir Fry Noodles (Chicken) – A flavorful and hearty dish. The noodles were cooked perfectly and packed with savory notes. We really enjoyed this one.
🍰 Desserts: A Sweet Finish
Japanese Cheesecake – Light, fluffy, and delicately sweet. It was a delightful way to end the meal. The presentation was also spot-on.
Molten Chocolate Cake – Rich, gooey, and absolutely indulgent. The chocolate oozed out perfectly, and it was a hit among all of us.
⭐ Service & Overall Experience
The service at Kofuku was exceptional. The staff was attentive, knowledgeable, and helped guide us through the menu with genuine warmth. Everything — from the food and drinks to the ambiance and hospitality — was top-notch.

Overall Rating: 🌟 10/10

If you're a fan of Japanese and Korean cuisine, Kofuku is a must-visit. With multiple outlets across India, it's easily accessible — but the Andheri West branch stands out for its vibe, flavor, and experience. We were a group of 10 looking for an indulgent seafood and coastal meal in Mumbai and Coast & Bloom delivered beyond expectations. With a modern, minimalistic ambience and a menu that is curated Malvani inspirations and there were some mains like Chettinad, konkani and goan, this spot is perfect for both celebrations and leisurely meals.

What We Ordered

Our feast included a fantastic mix of seafood, meats, and sides:

- Crab Kakori

- Shallow Fried Malvani Bombil

- Chicken Chilli

- Chicken Malvani Masala

- Prawns Bhujane

- APC Pomfret & APC Crab

- Pasta Arrabiata for kids

- Rice Bhakri, Ghavane, Wade

- Solkadi

Everything was rich, flavorful, and well-prepared, especially the seafood, which was fresh and cooked to perfection.

Service Excellence

Special shout-out to Chandani, Chandan, and Roshan, they took exceptional care of us from start to finish. For a table of 10, the service was quick, warm, and always attentive. They made excellent suggestions and ensured every dietary need was handled with care.

Price & Value

Medium to high priced considering the generous portions and seafood quality. Value for money for group dining with great ambiance.

-Verdict

A must-visit for seafood lovers and anyone wanting a coastal food experience with a modern twist. USP :- Decent Decor, Lively Ambience, Live DJ, Delicious Food, Signature Cocktails @ reasonable prices

DECOR, AMBIENCE & SEATING

They have a full fledged bar which offers a wide variety of mocktails & signature cocktails to spoil you for choices.
The place offers indoor seating only which is compact in size, seating is well spaced out & comfortable.
The Bar is located in one corner, seating is spread in the middle while the DJ plays some peppy tracks on his console from the other end.
They have two large tv screens on both sides to enjoy live sports while you munch on tasty food & sip classic cocktails 🍸

OUR FOOD & DRINK ORDER

Veg Starters
* Stuffed Tandoori Aloo Nazakat
* Paneer kalimirch
* Crispy chilli lime potato
* Salted baby corn mushrooms broccoli
* Veg spring roll

Main Course
A) Indian main course
* Punjabi chana masala

B) Chinese main course
* Thai bamboo rice

DRINKS
Mocktail
Water Melon cooler

Cocktails
Guava Mary hai
Kafir orange blast
Downtown sangria
Downtown sour
Bull frog

FOOD & DRINKS REVIEW

Their Food delivers on all fronts in terms of quality, quantity, taste & presentation.

Their Signature cocktails are made using unique combinations, decent alcohol level & less ice which balances the drink perfectly (not too light or strong).

STAFF & PRICING
The Staff is well groomed, polite, attentive & well rehearsed with the menu to make you comfortable & your food experience delightful.

In terms of pricing this place scores really well as their prices are reasonable when you account for the food & drink portions served.

I have visited twice and had a decent experience on both occasions. The place gets busy in the evenings, so it is better to visit in the afternoon or early evening. When I went with my family at 9:30 pm, we had to wait for 20 minutes to get a table.

The restaurant has both indoor air-conditioned seating and outdoor seating. We chose outdoor seating as air-conditioned seating area was fully occupied. But the tables on the left side did not seem suitable for four people, they were comfortable for only two people.

During my visits, I tried Pav Bhaji, Watermelon Juice, Filter Coffee, Triple Schezwan Fried Rice, Masala Dosa, Veg Mille-Jullie, Roti, Jeera Rice, and Sizzling Brownie. The Filter Coffee was good. The Pav Bhaji was made less spicy for a younger diner and was prepared just right. The Triple Schezwan Fried Rice was very good with a lot of vegetables. Masala Dosa was tasty and filling for one person. Veg Mille-Jullie had a spicy and tangy taste that made it different. The Sizzling Brownie was nice, although the brownie was slightly undercooked. The Watermelon Juice was fresh and the Jeera Rice was good.

The food quality is good, the portions are reasonable, but the prices are slightly high. The service is slow and we had to ask more than once for basic things like spoons or water.

Ratings:
Quality - 4/5
Quantity - 3.5/5
Service - 2.5/5
Price - ₹600 for 2 people

An iconic Mumbai café with a lively vibe and historic charm. Great place to relax after Colaba Causeway shopping—food is decent, drinks are good, and the atmosphere is the real highlight.

Leopold Cafe is worth visiting for its history and energetic ambience. The food is average for the price, but the experience, crowd, and location make it a must-visit spot in South Mumbai.

Very vibrant and famous place with lots of character. Can be crowded and slightly overpriced, but still worth a visit at least once for the iconic Mumbai café experience.

📍 About the Place
Leopold Cafe is one of Mumbai’s oldest and most famous cafés, founded in 1871 and located on Colaba Causeway — right across from the Colaba Police Station. It’s a cultural landmark as well as a popular hangout for tourists, locals, and fans of the novel Shantaram.

The café also carries historical significance because it was one of the spots attacked during the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks, and some bullet marks remain preserved as a memorial.

🍽️ Ambience & Atmosphere
Vibe:
Lively, bustling, and full of character — a bit of an old-school vibe with a mix of retro and bohemian decor.

Great people-watching spot after a shopping stroll along Colaba Causeway.

Often packed, especially in evenings and weekends — queues are common

🍔 Food & Drinks — What People Say
Positives:
Wide, varied menu with continental, Indian, Chinese & bar food options.

Popular items include beer towers, shepherd’s pie, walnut pie, chocolate desserts, chicken wings, burgers and more.

Some reviewers have enjoyed refreshing drinks like Coke floats and milkshakes.

Cost:
Expect mid-range pricing — around ₹2500 for two people including drinks (approx.) with alcohol.

🧑‍🍳 Service & Crowd
What reviewers note:
✔ Friendly, helpful staff when it’s not crowded.
⚠ Can be slow or inattentive during peak hours.
⚠ Busy weekends and evenings often have lines and waiting times.

📌 Pro Tips Before You Go
This cafe is worth visiting for the experience and atmosphere, even if the food opinions vary.

Best to visit earlier in the day or on weekdays to avoid long waits.

Ideal spot if you enjoy beer, relaxed seating, and a lively crowd., name_person=DNB Travel Diaries & Trails}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA], GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,000–1,200, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Moderate noise, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Parking_is_unavailable, E:PARKING_OPTION_NO_PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Clearly_labelled_vegetarian_dishes, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_CLEARLY_LABELED_ITEMS]}, time_line=Edited 3 months ago, review=I visited again, a week later. The décor, infused with traditional Asian elements, such as vibrant pictures and colorful umbrellas, added a unique touch to the dining space.
Jain food is also available. There were many options to choose from the menu.

No meal is complete without desserts! We indulged in the Walnut Brownie, topped with a scoop of creamy vanilla ice cream and drizzled with chocolate sauce. While it was good, it didn't quite match the exceptional standards set by the preceding dishes.

Overall, our experience at Moea Moea was delightful. We visited Agrezi Dhaba on Saturday, 31st May 2025, as a group of 3 married couples along with 2 kids, hoping for a pleasant evening out. Unfortunately, the experience turned out to be an utter disappointment from start to finish.

First of all, imagine walking into a restaurant on a Saturday night and seeing only two waiters managing the entire floor. That alone sets the tone for what’s to come. Service was painfully slow and chaotic, with one waiter literally sprinting from table to table trying to handle everything. It felt like watching a poorly managed event, not a professional dining experience.

I had made a booking through Zomato, only to be told by the waiter that pricing would differ if we paid via the app compared to paying directly. Why play such shady pricing games with customers? This kind of misleading marketing is simply unacceptable.

To make matters worse, some of my friends ordered from the bar, only to be told they were out of Blenders Pride by 9:30 PM. On a Saturday night? That’s basic stock management gone wrong.

Then came the confusing bar menu experience. The waiter actually insisted we decide how many pegs we were going to drink upfront because only then we’d be given a certain rate. Who does that? It’s ridiculous to expect guests to decide their entire order before even settling in. The pricing for single, 6-pegs, and 12-pegs was all over the place and made no sense at all.

The hospitality was shockingly poor. Since we had two young kids, we requested Wi-Fi so they could watch cartoons while the adults had dinner. There was no mobile network coverage, and the Wi-Fi was denied. The reason? According to the manager, sharing Wi-Fi would crash their system. Honestly, it was laughable—we actually joked about it being the “joke of the year.” This level of excuse-making is unprofessional at best.

If all this wasn’t enough, the waiter later rushed us to make the payment, standing by our table repeatedly asking “Google Pay ya cash?” When I asked for 5 minutes, his response was: “Jaldi karo, mujhe bhi ghar nikalna hai.” Absolutely unacceptable. We were still wrapping up our night and he made it feel like we were being kicked out. If there’s a rule that bills must be settled before midnight, then inform guests clearly in advance—not after pressuring them in the middle of their meal.

As for the food, it was bland, overpriced, and underwhelming. For a bill of ₹8500, we expected much better quality and taste. It felt like basic food dressed up with fancy pricing.

In short, Agrezi Dhaba completely ruined our Saturday night outing. Poor service, rude staff, lack of basic amenities, and average food at inflated prices.

["{guided_block={}, time_line=a month ago, review=We opted for buffet here and The primary positive point of our visit was the impressive variety and quality of the dishes offered on the buffet and the ambience. The few Indian dishes available were noted for being flavorful and well-spiced, demonstrating skill across different culinary styles. Had the dining environment matched the quality of the food, this would have been a five-star review and a location we would frequent.

But, there are Major Cleanliness and Hygiene Failure
Unfortunately, the entire experience was severely compromised by unacceptable issues with cleanliness and hygiene in the dining and buffet area. 👥 Crowd Density: Imagine cramming three busloads of people into a broom closet. That’s the vibe. You can’t move, can’t breathe, can’t even lift your hand to sip your drink. Fire safety clearly never crossed management’s mind.

🍹 Drinks & Food Service: If you’re into waiting 45 minutes for a watered-down cocktail and another hour for soggy finger food, this is your paradise. The bar staff moved slower than dial-up internet, and the kitchen seemed to be on strike.

🚨 Grand Finale: Police Raid: Just when people thought it couldn’t get worse—surprise! Police stormed the place. Lights on, music cut, everyone herded out like cattle. And here’s the kicker: because of the insane delays in serving, we hadn’t even used up their exorbitant cover charge. Basically, we paid for the privilege of standing in a sweaty, overcrowded box before being kicked out early.

👎 Overall: A masterclass in how to ruin a night out. Unjust cover charges, suffocating crowd, incompetent service, awful music, and the cherry on top—a raid. The only thing intoxicating here is the sheer incompetence.

Final verdict: If you want to burn your money while being miserable, this is the place. Otherwise, avoid like the plague.

reviews:

It is one of those restaurants in Borivali that continues to feel like home because of its food and hospitality.

This time, we began our meal with a bowl of Chicken Manchow Soup. It was served hot, and I enjoyed how it had a bold, flavorful taste without being overpowering. For starters, we ordered Veg Seekh Kebab, Mutton Seekh Kebab, and Chicken Pahadi Tikka. The Veg Seekh Kebab was nice, cooked well, and had the perfect earthy flavour. The Mutton Seekh Kebab was outstanding. It had a silky texture, was well-seasoned, and paired beautifully with the chutney. It was not chewy at all, and I really liked how smooth it felt with every bite. The Chicken Pahadi Tikka was equally good. The chicken was tender, juicy, and cooked with a light smokiness that made it enjoyable.

For the mains, I ordered Jeera Rice with Dal Tadka. The dal had a nice garlic tempering with the right amount of cumin, and together with the rice it felt wholesome and comforting. The Chicken Tikka Masala came with soft pieces of chicken in a thick gravy that had a good balance of spices. It went really well with the Tandoori Roti, which was crisp on the edges and soft in the middle. The Chicken Triple Schezwan Fried Rice was the last dish. It was mildly spiced, had a smoky taste from the wok, and the flavours were balanced in a way that made it enjoyable till the last bite.

It was the highlight of the evening. The chicken inside was fresh and well-cooked, and every bite reminded me why I have loved this dish here for years.

The food at Silver Coin Family Restaurant and Bar is consistently good, and the staff make the experience even better. They are polite, attentive, and always welcoming. After a few deliberations we zeroed in on 90ML Bar and Kitchen at Bandra, not far from Chetna college. It took us a couple of minutes to find the place even though Maps indicated that we had arrived, as the outlet is placed in a pretty non-descript row of low-rise buildings. We entered to find a small outdoor seating area, and chose to dine inside, away from the heat. Activating our Zomato Gold, we went along with the suggestion of our attendant and ordered the Classic variant of Long Island Iced Tea along with Peri Peri Peanuts. For starters we opted for Paneer Dragon Dry and Roast Chicken Chilly. The cocktail arrived first, and it was made to perfection. I highly recommend it, being one of the best LIIT's I have had in a long time. The peanuts were quite spicy as well as tangy, making for some great chakna. The starters then were served simultaneously, the vegetarian being, as expected, the milder of the two. Neither the paneer nor the chicken left any room for disappointment, being tender and appropriately chewy. Our second drink was Sex On The Beach, a concoction of vodka, schnapps, orange and cranberry juices. Not that I didn't like it, but I found it to be a bit fruity, would have preferred it to have some more punch. Continuing our Oriental theme for the food, we inquired about the rice preparations on offer, and Mongolian Rice appealed to us the most. Fried rice with finely chopped chillies and green gravy full of veggies like broccoli, capsicum, onion etc, it made for a very fulfilling main course. The desserts menu was rather limited, and our choice, Brownie with Ice Cream, wasn't available so we settled for Caramel Custard. It had a lovely jelly-like texture, but was not as sweet as expected nor did the chocolate sauce enhance the dessert, not a must have in my opinion. To sum up then, 90ML Bar and Kitchen ticks most of the boxes and does a good job without being exceptional. The only criticism I have is the service, which was a little lethargic at times. Basics like providing water and cleaning the table had considerable delays even though most of the tables were unoccupied. Overall, the drinks are nice, the food is on the spicier side and they seem to use chillies instead of masala to spice things up, I like that.
